sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 1: An ICU sepsis predictor serves elderly patients with 12 percent sepsis prevalence and young adults with 3 percent prevalence. The hospital demands both Equalized Odds and Predictive Parity simultaneously. Why is this mathematically impossible? Select Option A, B, or C above me!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: 12 percent elderly prevalence versus 3 percent young adult prevalence, and the contract demands both Equalized Odds AND Predictive Parity! Apply Bayes' theorem and select Option A, B, or C above me!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Spot on! That is Chouldechova's Impossibility Theorem. By Bayes' Theorem, when Equalized Odds holds the FPR-to-TPR ratio fixed across cohorts whose base odds differ by a factor of four—7.33 versus 32.33—the Positive Predictive Value calibration must diverge unless the classifier makes zero errors!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Careful! Neither larger sample sizes nor high AUROC can bypass Bayes' rule. Under Chouldechova's Impossibility Theorem, whenever base prevalences differ across groups, fixing the FPR-to-TPR ratio under Equalized Odds mathematically forces Positive Predictive Value calibration to diverge unless TPR equals 1 and FPR equals 0!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 2: A fintech credit model removes race and ZIP code yet yields Disparate Impact Ratio 0.58, uses human reviewers who agree 98.4 percent of the time, and executes SQL DELETE on consent withdrawal. sentences.text: No race column, a 98.4 percent human rubber stamp, and SQL DELETE on consent revocation—yet Fairness, Accountability, and Autonomy all fail! Choose Option A, B, or C above me to diagnose why!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Precisely correct! Redundant proxy features carry mutual information I of X and G greater than zero, defeating naive feature blinding. Rubber-stamping triggers Automation Bias and moral crumple zones. And SQL deletion leaves memorized gradients delta theta inside weights, demanding SISA machine unlearning!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Not quite! A Disparate Impact Ratio of 0.58 violates the EEOC 0.80 threshold because correlated features reconstruct demographics; 98.4 percent human agreement signals Automation Bias rather than meaningful oversight; and SQL DELETE never erases gradient updates already memorized inside model weights!
